A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Posterior Agreement robustness framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable; v2 retains Appendices A–E and adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and experiments on CIFAR-10 adversarial robustness, DiagViB-6 domain generalization and model selection, and IMDB perturbations, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds APGD/FAB evaluations on CIFAR-10 and APGD evaluations on ImageNet in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The Gibbs-posterior construction, factorized agreement kernel, optimization over beta, and PA-based model selection remain unchanged. The new background discussion and replacement of score notation R with S do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix F add ImageNet evaluation, extending adversarial coverage from CIFAR-10 to higher-resolution, 1000-class images. CIFAR-10 also gains APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, and FAB attack scenarios. DiagViB-6 and the appendix IMDB experiments are retained.

E2.justification: AFR_T remains the comparison measure. The six CIFAR-10 model/defense families, ERM/IRM/LISA discriminability comparison, and ERM/IRM model-selection comparison are unchanged. ImageNet uses four already represented model/defense families; the added attacks generate evaluation conditions rather than competing robustness measures.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate 10,000 randomly selected ImageNet validation images processed at 256 × 256 pixels and introduce AutoAttack procedures. Appendix F specifies bounds of {2,4,8,16,32}/255 for CIFAR-10 and {2,4,8}/255 for ImageNet. Existing PGD/FMN budgets and domain-generalization splits remain. Section 4.1 inconsistently writes denominator 225, whereas Appendix F and the figures use 255.

E4.justification: Appendix F substantially extends robustness testing across attack families, perturbation bounds, and attacked-sample proportions. These analyses examine whether PA/AFR discrimination and rankings persist under substantially more successful attacks. The earlier confidence-distribution, IMDB perturbation, and feature-alignment analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing predictive-confidence standard errors and dataset-seed descriptions are retained. v2 introduces no repeated-run counts, new uncertainty-estimation practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the added evaluations.

E6.justification: Figures 14–18 add substantial PA and AFR_T results for the new attack conditions and ImageNet. They show, for example, weak models reaching minimum PA at partial adversarial ratios and different ranking transitions under AFR_T. Previously reported plotted data and all three tables are unchanged; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The maximum-entropy derivation, posterior factorization, agreement formula, and three stated properties retain the same mathematical content. Appendix A preserves the proofs, with notation changes rather than substantive corrections or new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains PA-based robustness assessment without supervision, including model selection. v2 modestly qualifies its compliance claim: the introduction presents deliberately nonformal ideal properties and says PA 'better complies,' while the conclusion emphasizes reliable scoring rather than explicitly asserting consistency with the desiderata.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges difficulty separating covariate shift from sampling noise. Section 4.2 changes the interpretation from PA being more suitable than AFR_T to the measures providing complementary insights. It also adds interpretations of the new attack results and further justification for Adam; the finite-hypothesis and uniform-prior limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 reports approximate beta-optimization time of tens of minutes on one GPU and adds AutoAttack implementation information. It clarifies training from scratch, resampling across shortcut configurations, and epoch-wise model selection without establishing changes to the retained experiment. Existing code links remain; Figure 1's revised caption no longer specifies the earlier simulation size of 1000.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial positioning within the PA literature, tracing Approximate Set Coding, the similarity approach, Gibbs-posterior variants, and earlier applications. Section 3.1 distinguishes the original framework from this robustness adaptation. Additional references cover that lineage, annealing, AutoAttack/FAB, and ImageNet.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, experimental explanations, discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. v2 adds a Background subsection, reorganizes the PA explanation, and replaces 'metric' with 'measure' throughout. These changes extend beyond the prose needed to report new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds five multipanel figures, Figures 14–18. Figure 7 is enlarged and rearranged into five rows of paired plots, Figure 2 moves from the introduction to methodology, and Figures 1–2 receive expanded captions. Existing plotted data and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The APGD/FAB stress tests and ImageNet evaluation substantially strengthen the empirical basis for PA's robustness-assessment claims. They address v1's restricted adversarial validation by testing stronger attacks spanning broad failure rates and a much larger classification setting. Clearer PA research positioning and more qualified interpretation also improve the paper. The new attack-bound inconsistency limits protocol precision but does not outweigh these substantial validation gains.
